hdi.source: Kerala Human Development Report 2005 (State Planning Board / UNDP)
hdi.vintageWarning: THIS IS A 2005 FIGURE — about two decades older than the economic data in this file. It is the latest official district-level HDI for Ernakulam that could be sourced; Kerala has not published a comparable district HDI series since. Treat as historical context, not a current indicator. stateBest/stateAvg are deliberately omitted so that no current gap-closing target is computed from a stale value.

keySectors: Port, container transshipment and maritime logistics (Cochin Port, Vallarpadam ICTT)
Shipbuilding and ship repair (Cochin Shipyard Ltd)
IT and IT-enabled services (Infopark Kochi, Cochin SEZ)
Fertilisers and industrial chemicals (FACT — Udyogamandal and Ambalamedu)
Tourism — Kerala's top district for both domestic and foreign visitors
Spice trade (Spices Board of India headquarters, Kochi)
Marine products trade (MPEDA headquarters, Kochi; Kochi is India's 3rd-largest seafood export port)
Plantation crops — rubber (the district's largest crop by area) and coconut
strengths: Highest GDDP of any Kerala district: Rs 1,67,662 Cr at current prices (2024-25 Q), with per capita NDDP of Rs 4,15,797 against a Kerala average of Rs 3,08,338
Literacy 95.89% (male 97.36%, female 94.46%) with a female literacy rate above 94% — among the highest of any Indian district
Cochin Port handled 37.75 million tonnes of cargo in FY 2024-25, up 3.94% year-on-year, across 1,265 commercial vessel calls
Vallarpadam ICTT (DP World Cochin) set a record 834,665 TEUs in FY 2024-25 including 169,562 TEUs of transshipment, against a post-expansion capacity of about 1.4 million TEUs
BPCL Kochi Refinery: 15.5 MMTPA installed capacity running above nameplate — 17.22 MMT throughput at 111.11% utilisation in FY 2024-25
Cochin Shipyard Ltd: Rs 4,820 Cr consolidated turnover and Rs 827 Cr consolidated PAT in FY 2024-25; builder of INS Vikrant, India's first indigenous aircraft carrier
Infopark Kochi: 582 companies, 70,000+ professionals across 9.2 million sq ft on 323 acres, with IT exports of Rs 11,417 Cr in FY 2023-24 (up 24.28%)
Cochin International Airport (CIAL): 1.12 crore passengers, 65,651 MT cargo, Rs 1,142 Cr revenue and Rs 489.84 Cr net profit in FY 2024-25; the world's first fully solar-powered airport
Kochi Metro Phase I: 28.125 km and 25 stations, with FY 2024-25 ridership of 3.56 crore and an operating surplus of Rs 22.94 Cr in FY 2023-24
FACT posted Rs 4,050.91 Cr revenue and Rs 41.23 Cr net profit in FY 2024-25, with an all-time-high ammonium sulphate output of 250,578 MT
Cochin Special Economic Zone at Kakkanad: 132 operating units on 41.68 hectares
Kerala's top tourism district — 43.30 lakh domestic and 2.69 lakh foreign visitors in 2024
Headquarters of both the Spices Board of India and MPEDA, giving the district national institutional weight in spice and marine trade
challenges: Brahmapuram waste crisis: roughly 8.5 lakh MT of legacy waste across 100 acres; the March 2023 fire smouldered for 12 days and the NGT imposed a Rs 100 Cr environmental compensation on Kochi Corporation. Only about 40% of legacy waste had been treated by June 2024, and a 2024 fire-safety audit found hydrants and water-spraying systems non-functional
Coastal subsidence and flood risk: Kochi is projected to subside at 10-20 mm/year, with flooding potentially increasing 21% and covering 24 km² by 2100 (ISRO SAC study)

Coastal erosion: sea level off Kochi rose 1.8 mm/year (1971-2007) and about 30 km of the district's coast is affected, with Chellanam, Fort Kochi, Manassery-Kannamali and Nayarambalam identified as hotspots
Saltwater intrusion into coastal aquifers, with elevated salinity and alkalinity recorded at Chellanam, Edavanakkad and Pallippuram

Traffic and modal collapse: public transport's share of trips in Kochi fell from 83% in 2001 to 49% by 2015, with private vehicles now carrying about 89% of trips; NATPAC identified 10 severely congested junctions in 2023

Industrial pollution along the Eloor-Edayar stretch of the Periyar: sediment manganese up to 675.6 mg/kg and total chromium up to 750.6 mg/kg, with a mass fish kill in May 2024 prompting a CPCB call for a joint investigation
Near-total collapse of paddy cultivation: paddy fell from 57.53% of net sown area in 1980-81 to 5.39% by 2011-12, with about 75,189 ha and 108,456 t lost since 1957-58 — roughly a 90% decline
Continuing paddy-land conversion: 1,649.86 ha converted between 2018-19 and 2024-25, and Ernakulam accounts for 72,050 settled conversion applications, about 17% of the state total
Kochi Metro remains loss-making at the bottom line — a Rs 433.49 Cr loss before tax in FY 2023-24 despite an operating surplus
No current official district-level HDI exists for Kerala districts; the latest sourceable Ernakulam value dates from 2005
Cochin Port's stated cargo capacity is inconsistent across sources (78.6, 79.9 and 80.5 MMT all appear), making utilisation hard to assess
opportunities: Grow transshipment share at Vallarpadam ICTT — throughput of 834,665 TEUs sits well below the ~1.4 million TEU capacity, and transshipment is still only about 20% of volume
Expand petrochemical and downstream capacity around the BPCL refinery, which is already running above nameplate
Green shipbuilding and ship repair at Cochin Shipyard, building on its defence and commercial order pipeline
Scale the IT base beyond Infopark's current 582 companies and 70,000 professionals, using Kochi Metro Phase II (11.2 km Pink Line to Infopark) to link housing and workplaces
Complete Kochi Metro Phase II and rebuild public transport mode share from its 49% low
Convert Brahmapuram from liability to asset through completed legacy-waste biomining and waste-to-energy capacity
Coastal protection and managed retreat planning for the ~30 km of eroding shoreline, informed by the ISRO SAC subsidence projections
Marine value addition — Kochi is already India's 3rd-largest seafood export port (1,81,400 MT worth Rs 6,120.10 Cr in FY 2023-24) with room to move up the processing chain
Spice value addition and branding, leveraging the Spices Board headquarters presence
Cruise and MICE tourism building on Kerala's top district tourism position and CIAL's international connectivity
Periyar river remediation along Eloor-Edayar, which would unlock riverfront land and reduce health burden

dataCompleteness.verificationNote: Demographics, district GDDP/NDDP/per capita income, and the financial and operating metrics of the major assets are sourced from company reports, government statistics or credible press coverage. Sectoral GDDP composition is a state-average proxy. The HDI value is from 2005 and is flagged as stale. No roadmap, investment pipeline, credit, MSME or KPI-target tables are included because no verified district-level figures were available.

factualErrorsCorrected: 'IOCL Kochi Refinery, 7.5 MMTPA' — WRONG ON BOTH COUNTS. The refinery is owned by BPCL, not IOCL, and its capacity is 15.5 MMTPA, not 7.5 MMTPA.

'Cochin Port: 2nd largest port in India, 35 MTPA capacity' — the rank claim could not be substantiated and has been removed. Actual FY2024-25 cargo was 37.75 MMT; stated capacity is inconsistent across sources.

'HDI 0.784, rank 2/14, state best Thiruvananthapuram 0.821' — invented. The only sourceable district HDI is 0.801 with rank 1/14, from the Kerala HDR 2005. The Thiruvananthapuram figures did not exist.
'Per capita income Rs 5,36,055' and 'GDDP Rs 1,75,954 Cr' — unsourced estimates. Kerala DES reports per capita NDDP of Rs 4,15,797 and GDDP of Rs 1,67,662 Cr for 2024-25 (Q).
'State avg per capita Rs 4,20,000 (2026)' — invented. Kerala's per capita NSDP was Rs 3,08,338 in 2024-25.
'Cochin Shipyard: 3,000+ employees' — not verified and removed.

'Coir Board headquarters' listed as an Ernakulam asset — the Coir Board is headquartered in Kochi, but the '50,000 coir workers' and 'Rs 500 Cr turnover' district figures attached to it were invented.
removedInThisRevision: 'Spice exports Rs 400 Cr/year', 'seafood exports Rs 800 Cr/year, 40% of Kerala's', '1.5M+ annual visitors', 'Rs 2,500 Cr tourism revenue', '500+ houseboats', '15,000+ hotel rooms', '1.5M tourists', 'FACT 2,500+ workforce' — all unsourced district-level figures. Where real equivalents existed they have been replaced with sourced values (e.g. actual tourism arrivals, actual Kochi-port seafood export volume).
'Ship-breaking & recycling: 100+ vessels/year opportunity', 'floating solar on backwaters', 'offshore wind' — speculative items presented as pipeline.

roadmap / industries / creditData / msme / investments / kpis / roleDashboards blocks — these contained invented budgets, job counts, progress percentages and revenue projections presented with false source attribution and 'high' confidence labels. Removed rather than corrected.
